findings.title: No re-check of cache after taking the write lock (thundering herd)
findings.body: After the read-lock fast path misses, every concurrent caller that saw a nil cache serializes on `Lock()` and then re-reads the manifest file (and possibly makes an HTTP call) one by one. There is no second check of `entryPointAssetsCache` under the write lock. At startup, or after a failed load, N concurrent requests do N redundant loads while the others block. In Dev mode every call takes the exclusive lock and does file I/O under it, which serializes all requests that need web assets. Add a double-checked `if cfg.Env != setting.Dev && entryPointAssetsCache != nil` after `Lock()`.

findings.title: Cache overwritten with nil on error, and err may be masked
findings.body: `entryPointAssetsCache = result` runs even when `err != nil`, so a transient read failure (or a Dev-mode reload failure) replaces a previously valid cache with nil. Callers then get `(nil, err)`. This is existing behavior, but the lock now makes it a deliberate write path. Only assign the cache on success. Also, if the `cdn` branch fails, `err` is set and `result` is nil, and the file fallback then reassigns `err`, which is fine. A partial result is never cached, though, so the guard should be explicit.

findings.title: No concurrency test for the race fix
findings.body: The PR fixes a data race but adds no test, for example a `-race` test calling `GetWebAssets` from several goroutines. Nothing guards against a regression. Returning the shared `*dtos.EntryPointAssets` pointer is also still mutable by callers, and the code does not make it immutable.
